COMPLETE EMPIRICAL RESEARCH PLAN  

────────────────────────────────────────

1. Identification Strategy  
 Choice Staggered Difference-in-Differences (TWFE) complemented with an event-study specification.  
 Rationale Entry announcements occur at different calendar dates across routes. We observe routes both before and after the announcement, and many routes are never threatened. DID leverages within-route over-time changes while controlling for route-specific unobservables (via route FE) and economy-wide shocks (via time FE). An event study around the announcement isolates dynamic (anticipatory and post-announcement) effects and provides a built-in pre-trend test.

2. Treatment and Control  
 Unit of analysis incumbent‐airline i × origin-destination(OD) route r × month t.  
 Treatment variable Threat_ir t = 1 starting in the month an outside carrier first publicly announces its intention to serve route r and continuing until (i) actual entry, (ii) the announcement is withdrawn, or (iii) 12 months elapse (baseline definition).  
 Control group (i) Incumbent routes that never receive an entry announcement during the sample; (ii) “not-yet-treated” periods of future-threatened routes (used automatically by staggered DID).  
 Treatment timing / event date Month 0 = first press release or DoT filing that names the OD pair. Event-time d_k variables (k = -6,…,+12) are coded relative to this month.  

3. Key Identifying Assumptions  
A1 Parallel-trends: In the absence of an announcement, threatened and non-threatened routes would have evolved similarly.  
 Plausibility: Airlines do not usually pre-announce fare changes; routes of similar density/ distance behave comparably. We will bolster plausibility with rich controls (route-specific trends, fuel costs interacted with distance) and matched control routes.  
A2 No anticipation before the recorded announcement: Incumbents learn of entry only when the announcement becomes public.  
 Plausibility: DoT filings are generally the first verifiable signal; still, we will inspect pre-event coefficients (k < 0).  
A3 Stable unit treatment value (no spillovers across routes): An announcement on r does not directly alter prices on unrelated routes.  
 Plausibility: Some network spillovers are possible; we will test by adding carrier-level announced-elsewhere counts as controls.  

4. Main Threats & Mitigation  
T1 Endogenous announcement timing (demand spikes attract entrants).  
 Fix: Include route-specific linear trends; control for current demand proxies (load factor, GDP of endpoints); add competitor-level supply-side instruments in robustness (e.g., antitrust-related slot divestitures forcing entrants to expand).  
T2 Heterogeneous treatment timing with TWFE bias (negative weights issue).  
 Fix: Use the interaction-weighted estimator à la Sun & Abraham (2021) or Callaway & Sant’Anna (2021) rather than simple TWFE.  
T3 Multiple announcements / overlapping events.  
 Fix: Restrict sample to first threat per carrier-route or code only the earliest event; keep a clean event window.  

5. R Code Outline  

```r
# 0. Packages --------------------------------------------------------------
library(data.table)      # fast manipulation
library(fixest)          # TWFE & SA event study
library(did2s)           # Callaway-Sant’Anna robustness
setFixest_nthreads(4)

# 1. Load Data -------------------------------------------------------------
air <- fread("airline_route_month.csv")   # hypothetical filename

# 2. Variable Construction -------------------------------------------------
# convert dates
air[, date := as.Date(paste0(year, "-", month, "-01"))]
# Identify first announcement date per route
air[, first_announce := min(date[announcement == 1]), by = .(route)]
# Treatment dummy
air[, treated := (date >= first_announce)]
air[is.infinite(first_announce), treated := 0]  # never threatened
# Event-time (k)
air[, event_k := as.integer((date - first_announce) / 30.4)]
air[event_k < -6, event_k := -6]
air[event_k > 12, event_k := 12]

# 3. MAIN ESTIMATION -------------------------------------------------------
# Sun & Abraham event-study
est <- feols(price ~ sunab(first_announce, date, ref = -1) + control_vars,
             data = air,
             cluster = ~route,
             fixef = ~route + date)

etable(est, se = "cluster")

# 4. ROBUSTNESS: did2s implementation -------------------------------------
cs <- did2s(air,
            yname = "price",
            first_stage = ~ route + date,
            second_stage = ~ treated,
            treatment = "treated",
            cluster_var = "route")
summary(cs)
```
Notes:  
– `control_vars` may include oil-price × distance fixed effects, endpoint GDP, route-specific quadratic trend, etc.  
– For frequency outcome replace `price` with `flights`.  
– Cluster at route level; two-way (route and month) clustering available with `fixest`'s `cluster = c("route","date")`.

6. Expected Results  
Economic theory on limit pricing suggests incumbents cut fares and/or increase capacity to deter entry. Prior: A 5–10 percent decline in average real ticket price and a 5 percent increase in monthly flight frequency within six months of the threat. Effects should partially reverse if entry does not materialize.

7. Validity Checklist (Self-Assessment; 1 = satisfied, 0 = concern)  
C1 Evidence of parallel pre-trends…… 1  
C2 Correct functional form / no omitted interacted shocks…… 0.8  
C3 No treatment mis-classification…………………………… 1  
C4 Limited spillovers across units…………………………… 0.5  
C5 No differential measurement error across groups……… 0.9  

Overall score = 4.2 / 5.
